question: Do source-confirmed Method1 repeat-sampled reef-transects in the ten RLS regions occur next to distinct island shorelines, rather than only mainland coasts or single-island reefs?

frame.survey_method: physical metadata field methods contains numeric Method 1 token
frame.stable_site_key: RLS+country+area+location+site_code, max original coordinate range 0.01 degrees each coordinate
frame.eligible_site: at least one same-calendar-month consecutive-year Method1 survey pair with >=2 unique survey_id per year
frame.site_coordinate: median latitude and longitude from eligible site Method1 physical transects, never fish observations

marine_geography.individually_ambiguous_land_inside_point: Never infer that marine survey occurred on land; count separately
marine_geography.assign_to_island_if: marine point outside GSHHG land and <=5km of shoreline of exactly one unambiguous island, with mainland coast distance at least 1km farther than selected island
marine_geography.multi_island_region_condition: two or more different GSHHG island polygon IDs each with at least 3 distinct original strict Method1 repeat-sampled RLS site codes
marine_geography.marine_research_scope: reef metacommunity spatial network around islands, not observed land animal movement or island species extinction
marine_geography.origin: GSHHG shoreline does not identify oceanic versus continental geology or larval dispersal routes

outputs.scope: only 10 fixed RLS regions, per region aggregate surveyed site counts by nearest land type, source-locked polygon sha and number of multi-island networks

stop_go.if_under_two_geographically_distinct_mul: STOP cross-archipelago general island connectivity confirmation; may still investigate reef-patch metacommunity in separate ecological paper
